statement: Account timezone values require no deterministic trimming or casing correction before applying the deletion rule.
alternative: The general staging quality actions require automatically fixing "casing, whitespace trimming" and "standardize valid IANA timezones when pattern matches".
reason: Correctable timezone values would otherwise cause entire account records to be discarded.

statement: All non-null account timestamp and boolean values are directly castable to their declared output types.
reason: An invalid value could prevent the staging SQL and pipeline from executing.

statement: Twitter screen names containing harmful characters may be retained if removing those characters produces a nonempty name.
alternative: The description says "rows with NULL/blank or harmful characters are removed", which could require testing harmful characters in the original value.
reason: The interpretation determines whether potentially unsafe source records survive staging.

statement: A Twitter URL with a valid-looking prefix remains acceptable even when the rest of the value is not a valid URL.
alternative: The staging quality documentation describes nullifying an "optional URL fails regex", which may mean validating the whole field rather than a prefix.
reason: The unanchored ending can retain malformed optional URL values.

statement: All non-null Twitter profile timestamp and boolean fields used in direct casts are castable to the declared types.
reason: Malformed source values would make execution fail rather than produce cleaned profiles.

statement: Organic report account_id identifies the Twitter user whose profile should enrich the tweet.
evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on u.id = o.account_id and u.row_num = 1
alternative: The material index also exposes raw.tweet.user_id and raw.tweet.account_id; tweet.user_id could be the required profile join key.
reason: Using an account identifier as a user identifier can leave most profiles missing or attach the wrong users.

statement: raw.tweet.full_test contains the tweet text referred to as full_text in the contract.
alternative: The contract explicitly says "Tweet text joined from raw.tweet.full_text", while the material index lists only full_test.
reason: The implementation resolves a schema discrepancy without establishing the substitute field's meaning.

statement: Each tweet identifier has at most one matching row in raw.tweet after conversion to BIGINT.
evidence_of_dependence: left join tweets t on try_cast(o.organic_tweet_id as bigint) = t.tweet_id
reason: Duplicate matches would multiply report rows and their downstream metrics.

statement: The most recently synced Twitter profile is the intended profile for every report date, and no conflicting profiles tie at that sync time.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
alternative: The source is named twitter_user_history and reports contain date; the contract says only that user attributes are "joined from raw.twitter_user_history" without defining latest versus historical selection.
reason: Profile attribution can change across historical reports or become nondeterministic on ties.

statement: The organic tweet output should strip disallowed characters from raw user screen names rather than preserve the joined source value.
alternative: This model's screen_name description says "From raw.twitter_user_history.screen_name"; the explicit screen-name cleaning rules are specified separately for stg_social_media__twitter_user_history.
reason: This changes the reported identity text and can create empty names without the profile model's row filtering.

statement: Facebook staging impressions should use the maximum lifetime metric rather than the specified staging default of zero.
evidence_of_dependence: max(post_impressions) as impressions ... coalesce(pm.impressions, 0)::bigint as impressions
alternative: The contract defines impressions as "Default 0 in staging" and lists only post history and page data as this model's source tables.
reason: This introduces an additional source and changes a core performance metric for matched posts.

statement: Every qualifying Facebook post has at most one row in raw.facebook_pages_post_history.
alternative: The source includes updated_time and is named post_history, so multiple versions may require selecting a version.
reason: Repeated versions would produce duplicate posts and potentially retain outdated visibility states.

statement: The latest synced Facebook page record is the intended page metadata for all posts, regardless of deletion status.
evidence_of_dependence: partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last ... pg.row_num = 1
alternative: raw.facebook_pages_page_data includes _fivetran_deleted, which is not consulted when selecting page metadata.
reason: Deleted or historically inappropriate page versions could supply names and follower counts.

statement: A Facebook post with a null is_hidden value should count as visible.
alternative: The contract describes the model as "Published, visible Facebook posts" but does not define whether unknown visibility qualifies.
reason: This determines whether posts with unknown visibility enter reporting.

statement: Facebook post created_time and the numeric and boolean fields directly cast by this query contain only compatible values.
reason: An incompatible source value could abort the model rather than be corrected or nullified.

statement: Instagram metrics should select the first non-null media-specific field in a fixed priority order independent of the post's media_type.
alternative: The contract refers to normalized "mi.impressions" and other normalized metrics without defining this priority; the inspected rows contain simultaneous non-null carousel, story, photo/video, and reel metrics.
reason: The chosen priority can select the wrong metric family for most non-carousel posts.

statement: Each media identifier has at most one matching Instagram insights row across all source_relation values.
evidence_of_dependence: left join insights i on m.id = i.id
alternative: The insights table exposes both source_relation and _fivetran_id, but neither participates in the join or deduplication.
reason: Multiple matches would multiply posts and metrics.

statement: Each qualifying Instagram media identifier occurs only once in media history.
alternative: The history source includes _fivetran_id and _fivetran_synced, but no media-version selection is performed.
reason: Multiple historical versions would create duplicate post outputs.

statement: The latest synced Instagram user record supplies the intended account metadata for every historical media post.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
alternative: The contract requests account details "from user history" but does not specify latest rather than post-time values.
reason: Account names, follower counts, and media counts can differ materially across versions.

statement: Instagram media user_id and user-history id identify accounts in the same identifier namespace.
evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on m.user_id = u.id
alternative: The material index exposes both id and ig_id in Instagram user history, and their relationship to media user_id has not been checked.
reason: A namespace mismatch would remove account enrichment from otherwise valid posts.

statement: LinkedIn post_message should prefer article_title, then media_title, and use commentary only as a fallback.
alternative: The contract lists post_message without defining this priority; the available history source contains commentary, which could instead be the post message.
reason: The priority can replace the actual post commentary with a content title.

statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching post-content row.
evidence_of_dependence: left join raw.linkedin_pages_post_content pc on pc.post_id = regexp_replace(o.ugc_post_id, '^urn:li:share:', 'urn:li:share:')
alternative: The content source includes media_id and _fivetran_id, which could distinguish multiple content items for one post.
reason: A post with multiple content items would be emitted multiple times.

statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching UGC history row.
evidence_of_dependence: left join raw.linkedin_pages_ugc_post_history h on h.id = o.ugc_post_id
alternative: The source is a history table with last_modified_time and _fivetran_synced, but the query selects no single version.
reason: Multiple versions would duplicate posts and produce conflicting messages or timestamps.

statement: LinkedIn organization-post identifiers can be matched literally to history and content identifiers without reconciling share and ugcPost URNs.
alternative: The samples show organization-post IDs beginning "urn:li:share:" and history IDs beginning "urn:li:ugcPost:"; the implemented replacement leaves the identifier unchanged.
reason: Unreconciled identifier forms could leave messages and creation timestamps missing across many posts.

statement: LinkedIn organization-post records with null organization identifiers should be deleted from staging.
alternative: The contract declares organization_id as VARCHAR without a not_null constraint or delete_row rule.
reason: This adds an undocumented row-exclusion rule.

statement: The maximum channel_subscribers across all YouTube channel-basic records is the intended subscriber count for every video on that channel.
evidence_of_dependence: select channel_id, max(channel_subscribers) as channel_subscribers ... group by channel_id
alternative: The channel-basic source includes date, while the contract specifies only "COALESCE(channel_info.channel_subscribers, 0)" and does not define maximum-over-time selection.
reason: A historical maximum can systematically overstate subscriber counts.

statement: Each qualifying YouTube video identifier occurs only once in raw.youtube_video.
reason: Duplicate source identifiers would produce duplicate videos and metrics.

statement: All YouTube publication timestamps and numeric metric values used by the query are compatible with its casts and arithmetic.
reason: Malformed values could prevent pipeline execution.

statement: A missing YouTube channel title should produce the literal page_name 'Unknown Channel'.
alternative: The contract declares page_name as VARCHAR but provides no default or correction rule for it.
reason: This changes only the labeling of records with missing titles.

statement: The earliest tweet_created_at in each Twitter group equals the earliest report date required for created_timestamp.
alternative: The contract specifies "created_timestamp: earliest date in the group"; staging exposes date separately from tweet_created_at.
reason: Tweet publication time and report date can differ, changing timestamps and downstream date-based reporting.

statement: LinkedIn interaction metrics can be treated as absent for every staging record and therefore replaced with constant zeros.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(0, 0)::integer as clicks, 0::integer as impressions, 0::integer as likes, 0::integer as shares, 0::integer as comments
alternative: The reporting contract says metrics are "set to 0 when null; integers are otherwise preserved", although the minimal staging schema does not declare these metrics.
reason: This resolves a contract inconsistency by discarding any possibility of nonzero LinkedIn performance.

statement: A positive source engagement_rate is unavailable for every LinkedIn staging record, so its specified precedence requires no implementation.
evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then (clicks + likes + comments + shares)::double / impressions else 0.0 end as calculated_engagement_rate
alternative: The reporting contract requires "if the source engagement_rate is positive, use it", while the staging column list does not include engagement_rate.
reason: If source rates are intended to be supplied, the omitted branch changes all positive-rate records.

statement: Twitter screen_name, user_name, and account_id contain no whitespace-only values that must be treated as missing when choosing page_name.
alternative: The contract requires the "first non-blank" candidate and says "blank strings treated as missing"; whitespace-only strings could therefore require a trimmed emptiness check without trimming the retained value.
reason: Whitespace-only candidates can suppress valid fallback names and produce unusable canonical URLs.

statement: Facebook staging impressions always fit within the INTEGER range required by the reporting cast.
alternative: The staging contract declares impressions as BIGINT, whereas the reporting contract declares INTEGER.
reason: An out-of-range staging value would abort execution rather than produce the reporting table.

statement: Facebook impressions never contain negative values for which the contract requires division rather than a zero engagement rate.
evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then shares::double / impressions else 0.0 end as engagement_rate
alternative: The business logic says "engagement_rate is 0.0 when impressions are 0; otherwise" divide, although the denominator column description instead says "when greater than 0".
reason: Negative values expose a difference between the implemented guard and one explicit contract definition.

statement: Daily aggregated clicks plus likes, shares, and comments never exceed aggregated impressions when impressions are positive.
evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then (clicks + likes + shares + comments)::double / impressions else 0.0 end as engagement_rate
alternative: The daily contract requires "engagement_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1", while the YouTube contract defines both clicks and impressions as views and allows additional interactions.
reason: Groups exceeding this bound would violate the declared validation test despite implementing the stated ratio.

statement: Every recently dated intermediate record has non-null page_id and post_id.
alternative: The rollup declares not_null tests for both identifiers, but Facebook permits null page_id and Twitter and YouTube also permit null page_id.
reason: The rollup does not exclude or repair missing identifiers, so upstream nulls can violate its output contract.

statement: Pages with null page_id should be removed before creating retention cohorts.
evidence_of_dependence:
from page_activity
    where page_id is not null
alternative: The retention contract says to "only keep rows where created_timestamp is present" and defines cohorts "For each (page_id, platform)" without an identifier exclusion.
reason: Removing null identifiers can eliminate cohort weeks that the documented grouping would otherwise emit.

statement: Records without created_timestamp should be excluded entirely from monthly CTR reporting.
evidence_of_dependence:
from platform_posts
    where created_timestamp is not null
alternative: The business logic says "Union all posts" and "posts_count: number of rows (union-all, no de-duplication)", although the month column also has a not_null test.
reason: This resolves an undocumented missing-date policy by dropping records and their metrics.

statement: Records without created_timestamp should be excluded before daily aggregation and date-spine construction.
evidence_of_dependence:
from platform_posts
    where created_timestamp is not null
alternative: The daily business logic says to ingest all five models and normalize their dates without an explicit missing-date filter, while its output day has a not_null test.
reason: The choice affects whether undated activity participates in normalization and whether platforms with only undated activity appear.

statement: The rollup's recent-data windows permit future-dated posts without an upper date boundary.
evidence_of_dependence: created_timestamp >= current_date - interval '4 years' ... created_timestamp >= current_date - interval '2 years'
alternative: The contract says "keep the last 4 years" and "keep the last 2 years", which could instead mean a window ending at the current date.
reason: Future-dated records would enter the rollup and alter its rankings under this interpretation.
